title: 16-17. HE GAVE THEM FOOD IN EXCHANGE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Then bring your livestock,' said Joseph. 'I will sell you food in exchange for your livestock, since your money is gone.' So they brought their livestock to Joseph, and he gave them food in exchange for their horses, their sheep and goats, their cattle and donkeys. And he brought them through that year with food in exchange for all their livestock." — Gen 47:16-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The money is gone, so Joseph takes livestock instead. Notice what he does not do: he does not turn them away. "He brought them through that year with food." They survived, and Joseph kept them alive.

Some readers find this section of Genesis uncomfortable, and it is worth being honest about why. Over these verses the Egyptians progressively hand over everything they own. Was Joseph exploiting them?

The text itself does not condemn him, and the people will later thank him for saving their lives (v. 25). He is administering a state during a catastrophe of a scale we can barely imagine — seven years without harvest. Someone had to manage the only grain in the region, and without that management everyone starves.

But Scripture does not sanitise it either. It simply reports what happened, including the hard economics of it. That is characteristic of the Bible: it tells the truth about the world rather than tidying it up.

What we can say confidently is this — people who came with nothing left with their lives. In a far greater way, that is what God offers. Come, all you who have no money, and buy without cost (Isa 55:1). Christ gives what we cannot pay for.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you experienced God sustaining you through a season you thought you would not survive?
2. Why do you think Scripture reports difficult episodes without tidying them up?
3. What do you have that you could not pay for?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You sustain me through seasons I could not have survived alone, and that in Christ You give what I could never buy. Amen.
